title: 28 U.S.C. § 1652 — Rules of Decision Act
summary: Erie addresses the law a federal court uses when adjudicating rights governed by state law. Federal jurisdiction alone does not authorize creation of a federal general common law to replace state rules of decision.

sections.Role in the course: Erie addresses the law a federal court uses when adjudicating rights governed by state law. Federal jurisdiction alone does not authorize creation of a federal general common law to replace state rules of decision.
sections.What to examine: Identify the precise disputed rule and the competing federal source. If a valid federal statute or applicable Federal Rule governs, analyze its scope and authority. Otherwise use the assigned Erie line to consider state rights, likely forum incentives, and the relevant federal judicial interests.
